title: Gain staging for club rooms
hook: Red on the master, and the room hears amateur.
voiceover: Red on the master, and the room hears amateur. Nobody on the floor knows what a limiter is. They just feel that the hi-hats turned to sand and the log drum stopped hitting. That's clipping. What I actually do. Channel gains set so the loudest part of each record peaks around minus 6 on the channel meter, master at 0 and left alone all night. If the room needs to be louder, that's the sound guy's amp, not my master. When I bring a 2020s record mastered hot in next to a 1994 record mastered quiet, I fix it on the channel trim before it's live, not on the fader. What do you set your channels at?
caption: Midweek craft. Clipping doesn't sound like distortion to a crowd, it sounds like the DJ is bad. My rule: channel gains so each record peaks around minus 6, master at 0 and untouched all night, and volume is the sound engineer's job. Modern records are mastered much hotter than 90s records, so match them on the trim before they're live. DJs, where do you set your channels?
